1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the
Act"), filed by the petitioners men

tioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their Rajroop (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66169536/
1 land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose LAC no. 314/ 2016 (Award No.
16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 4//15 (416), 5//11 (416), 13//17 (4 16), 18 (416), 23/2 (204), 24 (416), 34//25 (400), 36//2/1 (208), 3 (4 16), 4 (416), 5 (204), 7 (415), 8(416), 9/1 (215), 12/1 (008), 13/1 (0 12) and 14/1 (010) i.e. total area measuring 58 Bigha and 04 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
LAC no. 314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
6. Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The land of the petitioner is situated in Village Mubarakpur Dabas and is well connected with metaled roads from all sides and at the time of acquisition was having great potential value as residential and commercial.

The land of petitioner is levelled and as such gives handsome crops income 2-3 times in a year to the petitioner and some part of the land is developed as colony and the petitioners also claims for loss of livelihood and also loss of income interalia on the following amongst other grounds.
Rajroop (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66169536/
2 ii)

sentences.text: The land of the petitioner is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Rohtak Road, Delhi and has great potential value as a perfect Building/ Commercial site.
Commercial and Residential activities have commenced all around the land of the petitioner and are going on since more than 12 years.
All kinds of civic amenities like electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college, etc are easily available to the land of the petitioners,
Thus, the land of petitioners has great value being developed and a perfect residential and commercial site.
LAC no. 314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 iii)
The Land of the petitioners is approachable by metaled road and is very close to Nangloi township and Mundka Industrial Area and the same were fully developed at the time of notification.

There are many residential colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Mir Vihar, Jain Colony and Rama Vihar,
etc which are existing since 1993 near the land of the petitioner and Govt. is also going to regularise the said buildings and provide all the civic amenities thereafter.
Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/- per sq. yards.

iv) The land of the petitioners have been covered by the other revenue estate such as Rani Khera,
Madan Pur Dabas, Karala and Mazri which are well developed by way of construction of colonies and have great potential value.
Moreover, the petitioners have solid proof regarding the higher market value of land which is not less than Rs. 10,000/- and the same may be produced at the time of evidence before the Court.

It is also alleged that the Government police has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong and illegal and the same should be ratify and compensation be paid to the petitioners.
v) The Government Policy has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong and illegal.
Further, the LAC has failed to consider to assessing the value of standing trees, tubewell and structures.
LAC no. 314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 7.

It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 10,000/- per sq.
yards and Rs. 5 lakhs for damages as sustained by compulsory acquisition and cost of boaring and structure be awarded alongwith statutory benefits and interest under LA Act and enhanced compensation be released to the petitioners and the category of land be rectified.
It is further prayed that the reference as to the inadequacy of compensation may kindly be referred to Ld. District Judge for adjudication.
Petitioners also prayed for the recovery of the cost of the petition alongwith any other order deemed fit and proper be also passed in favor of the petitioner.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the petition is not maintainable as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the present petition.

It is submitted that the ld. LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the said land prevailing at the time of Section of LA Act and also Rajroop (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66169536/
3

sentences.text: considering the existing locations, surroundings, availability of civic amenities and other resources.

The possession of the land in question measuring 12 Bigha and 00 Biswas as detailed in Statement U/s 19 of LA Act has been taken on 04.04.2006 and was delivered to DDA and as such DDA is also a necessary party being the beneficiary of the said land.
The petitioner has not brought any specific and cogent evidence on record to claim higher compensation.

All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted LAC no. 314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect LAC no.
314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

11. It is stated that the possession of the said land bearing Khasra No. 4/15 (416), 5/11 (416),
36/2/1 (208) has been taken over by the DDA on 04.04.2006 and after taking possession, the same was transferred to RPD VII.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
12.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 16.09.2014:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?

OPP.
2. Relief.

sentences.text: Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.

sentences.text:
However, no LAC no.
314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 12 specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsel for petitioner and UOI.
None had appeared on behalf of DDA to address the final arguments.
DDA even failed to file written submissions though opportunity was granted.
Therefore, this Court deems it fit to pass judgment on merits of the case.

My issuewise findings and determination are as under : 
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?

OPP.
15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the LAC no.
314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).

The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 21.

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No.
13//17 (416), 18 (416), 23/2 (204), 24 (416), 34//25 (400), 36/3 (416), 4 (416), 5 (204), 7 (415), 8(416), 9/1 (215), 12/1 (008), 13/1 (012) and 14/1 (010) has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
LAC no. 314/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajroop Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
